payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When the investigation runs, it shall establish a reproducible cold and warm release baseline and account for elapsed time, agent coordination, available token/tool costs, repeated checks, setup, packaging, hooks, pushes, CI queue/runtime and publication waits, with unknown quantities marked unavailable.
- When a delay is assigned a cause, the research shall cite the actual instruction or call path and demonstrate the causal mechanism or clearly label the remaining hypothesis. It shall distinguish required independent safety controls from redundant work over equivalent trusted inputs.
- When the baseline is established, the task shall record a measurable improvement target and implement the smallest supported changes, including canonical release guidance or orchestration when they cause the delay. A report alone shall not complete this task.
- When the improved process is tested, the actual final tagged candidate, release notes, install pins, uploaded artifacts and fresh consumer behavior shall remain verified. Dirty user work, canonical release ownership, immutable published tags, failure recovery and existing genuine approvals shall remain protected. No gate, test, check, cap or hook shall be weakened or bypassed, and no execution witness shall be fabricated.
- When before and after results are compared, they shall use comparable release cases and report complete elapsed time, sample size and limits. Moving work outside the measured interval or after publication shall not count as an improvement. The result shall demonstrate the recorded speed target while preserving safety.
- When changes affect tracker handling or telemetry, historical events shall remain append-only and independent tracker PRs shall still merge in either order without manual tracker conflict resolution or a main-into-branch merge required solely by tracker file changes. Prefer leaving the existing schema and Git merge behavior unchanged; exercise both merge orders if they change.

## Trigger

When cutting a verified release still takes substantial elapsed time and repeated coordination, I want to investigate the complete release path and implement the demonstrated improvements, so I can publish safely with less wall time and agent effort.

## Context

Requested after cutting, committing and pushing v0.27.0. The GitHub release is published and its published wheel passed a fresh consumer install/check/hooks-check/skills-check/uninstall run. This card is filing only now. Do not begin research or implementation until the user selects it.

Study the whole request-to-publication process, including agent deliberation, instruction retrieval, runbook coordination and gaps between commands. Do not assume shell execution is the only cost or that fewer checks alone mean a faster safe release. Examine the release command, release-process skill, verification engine, tutorial recording requirement, packaging, Git hooks, push behavior and GitHub workflows. Include permission and tracker-description friction if observed; establish causes rather than assuming them.

The current release exercised full verification on main and in a separate rehearsal clone before the cut, then on the new release trees. Both pushes reran full-mode gates while reusing the unit-test receipt. Record exactly why each execution ran, what it proved and whether its inputs were equivalent. Reuse existing mechanisms before adding another release orchestrator.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/release*.py`
- `src/basicly/capability_proof.py`
- `src/basicly/verify*.py`
- `src/basicly/pytest_inputs.py`
- `.basicly/core/skills/release-process/**`
- `.basicly/core/fragments/**`
- `.basicly/core/templates/**`
- `.scripts/*release*.py`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml`
- `docs/tutorial/first-loop.md`
- `docs/how-to/**`
- `tests/test_release*.py`
- `tests/test_verify*.py`

Refine this candidate scope from the research before changing code. Correct canonical YAML and regenerate agent surfaces if instruction wording or ordering is causal. Do not build a parallel instruction or release system.

## Evidence from v0.27.0

Tagged commit: 33d32739401a537a533ba43c30e25df26e685cfc. Release workflow: https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/actions/runs/40138579964 . Release: https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/releases/tag/v0.27.0 . The rehearsal and final release runtime files were identical. Their only tracked differences were a manifest generation timestamp and the release record citation in CHANGELOG.md.

The final main full verification artifact reports 212.733 seconds, including 130.475 seconds for the pytest process and 26.951 seconds for fresh/live ledger tests. Its output reports 7705 passed, one expected failure, and 185 ledger tests. Pre-push summaries report 49.08 seconds for main and 49.13 seconds for the tag even though both reused the verified unit-test result. These are individual observed samples, not a representative benchmark or a demonstrated root cause. Main-session token totals were unavailable.

Raw local evidence and verification receipts are archived under .basicly/usage/release-0.27.0. That ignored directory is machine-local; retain this card's measurements and public commit/workflow links as portable starting evidence. Include the release-record citation correction and tutorial-version ordering in the investigation. They required extra coordination during this cut.

## Related work

basicly-0m4thm1 covers general phase-cost reporting and repeated-verification reasons. basicly-s0snzge covers resumable landing and closure. Reuse their mechanisms where present; do not create an artificial dependency before the investigation establishes one.

Windows-specific mechanisms shall receive native consumer evidence or be explicitly left unverified. Reported tests and OS-neutral claims shall not substitute for demonstrated behavior.
- When an issue is confirmed, the investigation shall explain why existing tests, gates, platform coverage or instructions missed it, using the actual exercised condition and call paths. A policy change shall be identified separately from a bug fix.
- When the proposed solution is assessed, the review shall cover encoding and error handling, junction cleanup and user data preservation, program resolution, comment/docstring enforcement, interpreter requirements and quoting, and cross-platform regressions without weakening required gates or controls.
- When the evidence is complete, the story shall present a justified recommendation to merge, update/request changes, comment, or decline, with any proposed response drafted for review. No PR action or implementation shall occur merely because this investigation story was filed.

## Trigger

When PR #1 reports failures that our checks did not expose, I want an independent investigation of its claims and proposed changes, so I can decide whether they are valid, explain any coverage gap, and choose the appropriate PR response.

## Filing scope

Only file this story now. Do not investigate validity, implement changes, update the branch, comment on the PR, merge it or close it until the user selects this work. Keep the PR open and unchanged during filing.

## PR snapshot

URL: https://github.com/niksavis/basicly/pull/1
Title: fix(hooks): make hooks work on windows and scope no-comments to added lines
Head: fix/windows-hooks at a89e8f5f64394e5f745afd616539ddf8b9022bf7
Base: main
State at filing: OPEN

The description reports consumer problems on Windows 11 with Git Bash, uv 0.9.5, Store Python 3.12 on PATH and an existing Python 3.12 virtual environment. Its baseline is basicly v0.26.11. These are the author's claims, not findings established by this filing. Compare that baseline, the PR head and current main; re-fetch the current head and discussion before investigating.

## Claims to inventory and assess

- Text subprocess decoding in hooks reportedly fails on UTF-8 diffs under a Windows legacy code page and can surface a secondary identity-guard exception. Assess both the decoding failure and the safety of replacement decoding.
- Staged snapshots reportedly copy large environment directories when symlinks lack privileges, hit long-path failures and isolate usage writes. Assess the proposed junction fallback, target-preserving cleanup and failure behavior.
- Repository-relative check programs reportedly resolve incorrectly on Windows in normal execution and fix paths. Trace every affected caller and verify both platform path forms.
- The no-comments hook reportedly rejects existing comments in edited files despite wording about new additions. Assess the proposed added-line filter, new/untracked files, staged snapshots, renames and multiline docstrings. Separate a demonstrated defect from a proposed policy change; do not silently weaken the approved comment ban.
- Hook launchers reportedly select Python 3.12 despite the engine's Python requirement. Assess interpreter selection, existing consumer environments, the proposed fixed 3.14 request, standalone-kit compatibility, and the reported Lefthook Windows quoting/redirection behavior.
- Inventory the reported pre-existing Windows test failures separately, including foreign hook arguments/execution, initial commits and staged fixes, consumer exclusions, progress timing and other named install/upgrade cases. Check their relevance to accepting this PR rather than assuming the branch introduced or fixes them.
- Assess the smaller observations about terse hook errors, UV_NO_SYNC with no-project, imported identity fields and scrub, same-version wheel caches, and the reported isolated-versus-parallel comments-kit test behavior. Verify the PR's regression and end-to-end testing claims independently.

## Required research

Read the complete current description, issue and review comments, inline threads and every changed file. Map each claim to a reproducible case, actual call sites, current requirements and controls. Use native Windows consumer evidence for Windows-specific mechanisms, plus deterministic cross-platform controls where possible. Establish what remains unverified if native evidence is unavailable.

Explain why each confirmed issue escaped: missing platform coverage, fixtures that miss the consumer condition, insufficient assertions, instruction/policy ambiguity, environment assumptions, drift since the baseline or another demonstrated cause. Distinguish causation from correlation and a claimed test from proof that the condition was live.

After the evidence, recommend one disposition with reasons: merge as proposed, request/update specific changes, comment with findings or clarification, or decline/close. Separate technical validity from whether the proposed solution is safe and appropriate. Obtain any required concrete approval before an external PR action; this filing authorizes none.
